title: pravapis alphabet table
description: The Belarusian alphabet (data/chars/alphabet.tsv): one row per letter, lowercase and its single capital form. NORMATIVE for any implementation's word-character class and case handling. The tokenizer's word class (a run this project treats as one Cyrillic word) is exactly the `lower` column, plus the apostrophe class (apostrophes.schema.json) and a hyphen for joining; deliberately narrower than Unicode's general Cyrillic script property, which also matches Russian/Ukrainian letters this project's alphabet excludes (see src/pravapis/tokenize.py, is_belarusian_word). `lower`+`upper` together are also this project's case-fold table: an implementation should map a letter to its row's other column rather than trust its language runtime's own case conversion, because `str.casefold()` (Python) and `String.toLowerCase()` (JavaScript) are not guaranteed to agree on every Unicode range.

columns.name: lower
columns.description: The letter's lowercase form, and the form every rule pattern and lexicon entry is written in.

description: The alphabet, parsed: the ordered list of its rows.
x-constraints: `lower` is unique across rows, and so is `upper`: a letter appears exactly once, and no two letters share a capital form.
Order is the conventional Cyrillic alphabetic order; it has no effect on behaviour but keeps the file reviewable against a published alphabet chart.
